name: The Wealdmark
seat: the Weald Hold (upriver fortress-palace, unlisted in city records)
summary: The old kingdom upriver of Velkash: forest, orchard-country, and the Weavers' River's upper fords. The Wealdmark predates the Crown Re-set, claims pre-Sundering noble blood, and regards the Velkash Crown as merchants who bought a throne. Both are right.

government.title: Warden-King
government.current: King Emrys of the Old Weald
government.note: Hereditary; succession requires Septuary certification of lineage — which gives the tiny temple-state leverage over both river kingdoms.

population.note: largest greenfolk population outside the Greenwood; orchard-tenders by treaty

laws: Mirrors the Crown's Edict of Silence in public; enforcement is famously slower. Glimmerborn born in the Wealdmark have a way of emigrating before their name reaches a watchlist.

relations.note: Toll wars on the river; marriage negotiations as periodic ceasefires.
The orchard-treaty: greenfolk tend Wealdmark orchards, the kingdom keeps loggers out of the Greenwood.
Accords honored in writing; wardens complain the Wealdmark is 'soft country'.

history_notes: Claims continuity with a Concord-era river province — its archives burned in the Sundering, conveniently.
Sheltered Solmere refugees after 183 AA; never returned them to Censer custody.
adventure_hooks: A Wealdmark heir's lineage fails Septuary certification; proving the clerk forged it means entering Censer archives.
River tolls double; Velkash hires players to find an alternate route — through Greenwood treaty land.
An old Solmere refugee dies leaving a trunk of pre-Edict texts to 'the child of the orchard'.
